Define genetically modified. Because, afaik, crops have been genetically modified since the dawn of agriculture, when humans started putting seeds in the ground instead of letting nature do its thing.

There is quite some difference between hybridization and genetic modification. In regular cross pollination, the species being crossed have to be related, basically respecting their common evolutionary origin. Whereas with GMOs, you can take any gene from any species and splice it into a crop, for example you can put fish genes in tomatoes or the like.

Then there is the whole issue of GMO patents, but that's another story.
